failures.title: Mercedes M270 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: Early production M270 units are prone to timing chain stretch, leading to a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts and potential check engine lights indicating camshaft correlation errors. If ignored, the chain can skip teeth, causing catastrophic valve and piston interference.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit and tensioner replacement is viable. However, if the chain has already snapped or caused secondary internal damage, a full Mercedes M270 engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

items.title: Camshaft Adjuster Oil Leaks and Turbo Wastegate Rattle
items.whatHappens: The camshaft adjuster solenoids and valve cover gaskets can develop oil leaks, leading to low oil levels and potential engine damage if left unattended. Additionally, the turbocharger wastegate actuator can develop a rattle or fail, causing boost pressure faults and reduced performance.
items.repairVsReplace: Solenoids and gaskets are relatively inexpensive to replace as preventative maintenance. A failed turbocharger requires replacement or rebuilding, and if oil starvation has occurred due to leaks, a full engine rebuild may be necessary to address scored cylinder walls.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M270
variants.intro: The M270 engine code (including sub-codes M270.910 and M270.920) is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically near the bell housing or oil filter housing, and is clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Common Confusion Warning: Owners frequently confuse the M270 with the closely related M274. While they share the same 2.0-litre turbocharged architecture and internal components, the M270 is mounted transversely for front-wheel-drive compact models (A-Class, B-Class, CLA, GLA), whereas the M274 is mounted longitudinally for rear-wheel-drive platforms (C-Class, E-Class). Fitting an M274 as a replacement for an M270 will result in severe mounting, exhaust, and wiring loom incompatibilities.

relatives.description: - The longitudinal predecessor it replaced, which shares similar timing chain and balance shaft vulnerabilities but differs entirely in mounting orientation and accessory layout.

- The newer modular successor that dropped the transverse 2.0L layout in favour of a lighter 1.3L/1.4L configuration for compact models, though some late M270 applications overlapped with early M282 introductions.

- The longitudinal twin of this engine; owners of rear-wheel-drive C-Class or E-Class models with similar symptoms should look here instead, as the M274 is not a direct physical swap for the transverse M270.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Mercedes M270 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Mercedes M270 is only advisable for lower-mileage host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by a full service history proving the timing chain has been inspected and replaced if necessary. Without this history, the risk of inheriting the same stretch or oil leak issues is unacceptably high.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M270. A proper reconditioned unit will include a brand-new timing chain kit, updated tensioner, refreshed camshaft adjuster seals, and a tested turbocharger, directly addressing the engine's known weak points out of the box.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M270 suffered catastrophic timing chain failure that damaged the cylinder head, valves, or pistons. A specialist rebuild will machine the block, fit updated chain components, and upgrade all lubrication pathways to prevent a repeat failure.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing a replacement is only half the job. Our network provides full supply and fit services, ensuring the engine is installed by Mercedes-specialist technicians with a nationwide warranty backing both the labour and the unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For compact hosts like the W176 A-Class or W246 B-Class, current UK market values typically sit between £4,000 and £12,000. With a reconditioned M270 replacement costing from £3,800 (plus fitting), the repair cost can approach 50-80% of the vehicle's value on older or higher-mileage examples. Always evaluate the car's scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full engine replacement on sub-£6,000 hosts.

items.question: How much does a Mercedes M270 engine replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: A Mercedes M270 engine replacement typically costs between £3,800 and £6,500 for a reconditioned supply-only unit . Fitted costs generally add £650-£910 for independent specialist labour, and fully rebuilt units with upgraded components can reach £5,500-£8,500 supply-only. Compare M270 engine replacement quotes from vetted UK specialists.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Mercedes M270 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern for the M270 is timing chain stretch and tensioner wear, particularly in early production units, leading to cold-start rattling and potential check engine lights. Additionally, camshaft adjuster oil leaks and turbo wastegate rattles are common secondary issues that can lead to oil starvation or boost faults if ignored. Get quotes for a rebuilt M270 with these known weaknesses addressed.

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M270 engine?
items.answer: The M270 is fitted to Mercedes-Benz front-wheel-drive compact models from 2012 to 2018, including the A-Class (W176), B-Class (W246), CLA (C117/X117), and GLA (X156). It powers badges ranging from the A200 and A250 to the GLA200 and GLA250, and you should always verify your exact fitment via registration lookup. Confirm your exact M270 fitment before requesting a quote.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Mercedes M270 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M270 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known timing chain stretch and oil leak risks. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting the same latent defects unless accompanied by stamped proof of preventative chain replacement, whereas reconditioned units include updated chain kits, tensioners, and revised seals, providing a reliable long-term solution. View our reconditioned Mercedes M270 engine options with 12-month warranties.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the M270 and not the M274?
items.answer: The M270 engine code (including sub-codes M270.910 and M270.920) is stamped on the engine block near the bell housing or oil filter housing and is listed on your V5C registration document. It is commonly confused with the M274, but the M270 is mounted transversely for front-wheel-drive models, meaning fitting an M274 will result in severe mounting, exhaust, and wiring loom incompatibilities.
